findings_qualitative.value: 13CO peaks between the dust lane and the ring, unlike 12CO, which follows the dust lane and tidal tails.

evidence.quote: In contrast to $^{\rm 12}$CO, its line emission peaks between the dust lane and the circumnuclear molecular ring.

claims.hypothesis: Is the dust-lane gas diffuse and unbound while funneled inward?
claims.experiment: Mapped 12CO/13CO 1-0 ratio across the dust lane and nucleus
claims.result: Ratio >45 in dust lane, ~30 in nucleus
claims.finding: Gas in the dust lane is diffuse and unbound, then compressed in the inner 1.5 kpc

evidence.quote: This drop in ratio with decreasing radius is consistent with the molecular gas in the dust lane being kept in a diffuse, unbound state

claims.hypothesis: Does inflow dilute starburst isotopic enrichment?
claims.experiment: Used C18O upper limit and the line ratio to infer abundance ratios
claims.finding: Inflow of unprocessed gas may explain the low 18O enrichment

evidence.quote: We suggest that the massive inflow of gas may be partially responsible for the low $^{\rm 18}$O/$^{\rm 16}$O abundance

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Shocks and high gas temperature as the cause of the high ratio considered unlikely

evidence.quote: This most likely excludes the notion of high gas temperatures as the cause of the elevated line ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: Beam dilution may affect the C18O deficiency; higher resolution is needed.

evidence.quote: this could also be an effect of the size of the beam in the observations

referee_caveats_inferred: Abundance ratios rest on an assumed tau=1 for 12CO
The C18O limit is a lower limit on the abundance ratio only
